titleStmt.title: The Entropy Formula for the Ricci Flow and Its Geometric Applications
titleStmt.author: Grigori Perelman

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: The Entropy Formula for the Ricci Flow and Its Geometric Applications

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: In this paper we carry out some details of Hamilton program.

span.label: singularity formation in the Ricci flow
span.quote: In this section we present an application of the monotonicity formula (3.4) to the analysis of singularities of the Ricci flow.

span.label: mathematical-proof
span.quote: A rigorous proof of this monotonicity is given in the next section.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE SAME OBJECT HAS A NAME IN ANOTHER FIELD, AND THE PAPER SUPPLIES THE TRANSLATION: the functional's first variation formula CAN BE FOUND IN THE LITERATURE ON THE STRING THEORY, WHERE IT DESCRIBES THE LOW ENERGY EFFECTIVE ACTION - and THE FUNCTION f IS CALLED DILATON FIELD there. One mathematical object, two literatures, two names, and a citation offered so the reader can cross between them
span.note: about this quote: The span begins mid-sentence, at "and its first variation formula", because everything before it in that sentence is interleaved mathematics - "can be found in [H 4, § psi = (delta m)2 psi ... M gijRm R and its first variation formula". So the quote does not name WHICH functional, and the tag does not claim to. The translation it records - the same object called `dilaton field` in the string theory literature - is intact.
span.quote: and its first variation formula can be found in the literature on the string theory, where it describes the low energy effective action; the function f is called dilaton field

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A MATHEMATICAL FREEDOM IS EXPLAINED BY A PHYSICS TERM RATHER THAN A MATHEMATICAL ONE: THE REMARKABLE FACT HERE IS THAT DIFFERENT CHOICES lead to THE SAME FLOW, up to a diffeomorphism - THAT IS, THE CHOICE OF m IS ANALOGOUS TO THE CHOICE OF GAUGE. The invariance is named by importing a word from another discipline, and the import is what makes it recognisable
span.quote: The remarkable fact here is that different choices of m lead to the same flow, up to a diffeomorphism; that is, the choice of m is analogous to the choice of gauge.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE ANALOGY'S STATUS IS MARKED AS HEURISTIC IN ITS OWN NUMBERED REMARK, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS SPELLED OUT: HEURISTICALLY, this statistical analogy IS RELATED TO the description of the renormalization group flow - IN THE LATTER one obtains quantities BY AVERAGING OVER HIGHER ENERGY STATES, WHEREAS IN THE FORMER THOSE STATES ARE SUPPRESSED by the exponential factor. The resemblance is asserted and the point of divergence given in the same breath
span.note: about this quote: CONTEXT THIS QUOTE CANNOT CARRY, recorded because it is the paper's central terminological hedge. The sentence that states the analogy is SCRAMBLED in the staged text and cannot be quoted: "In this section we show that the functional a sense analogous to minus entropy. W , introduced in section 3, is in" - the clean reading is "the functional W, introduced in section 3, is in a sense analogous to minus entropy". Damage shape 5. **The TITLE of the paper says `the entropy formula`; section 5 says `in a sense analogous to MINUS entropy` - qualified twice, by the hedge and by the sign - and that sentence is the one the extraction destroyed.**
span.quote: Heuristically, this statistical analogy is related to the description of the renormalization group flow, mentioned in the introduction: in the latter one obtains various quantities by averaging over higher energy states, whereas in the former those states are suppressed by the exponential factor.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PROPERTY IS DISCOVERED AND IMMEDIATELY GIVEN A NAME BUILT FROM TWO OTHER NAMES: a REMARKABLE PROPERTY of solutions with nonnegative curvature operator IN ARBITRARY DIMENSION is CALLED A DIFFERENTIAL HARNACK INEQUALITY, and what it ALLOWS is stated in the same sentence - comparing the curvatures at different points and different times. The name records neither the property nor its use but its lineage
span.quote: Hamilton [H 3] discovered a remarkable property of solutions with nonnegative curvature operator in arbitrary dimension, called a differential Harnack inequality, which allows, in particular, to compare the curvatures of the solution at different points and different times.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A RESULT IS VALUED BY WHAT IT UNBLOCKS IN SOMEONE ELSE'S PROGRAMME: the theorem is said to REMOVE THE MAJOR STUMBLING BLOCK IN HAMILTON'S APPROACH TO GEOMETRIZATION. The contribution is located relative to another person's plan rather than stated on its own terms
span.quote: This result removes the major stumbling block in Hamilton’s approach to geometrization.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A QUESTION IS PROPOSED AND CALLED NATURAL, WHICH IS THE ONLY WARRANT OFFERED FOR IT: A NATURAL QUESTION IS WHETHER we have a gradient shrinking soliton WHENEVER S STAYS BOUNDED. The word NATURAL carries the whole justification for why this is the question to ask next, and no other reason is given
span.quote: A natural question is whether we have a gradient shrinking soliton whenever S stays bounded.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A TERM IS ATTRIBUTED TO A PERSON RATHER THAN DEFINED: a solution defined on a time interval of a certain form is ANCIENT, IN HAMILTON'S TERMINOLOGY - and the attribution is the definition's provenance, given in place of a criterion
span.quote: that is, we have an ancient solution to the Ricci flow, in Hamilton’s terminology

span.label: for general m the gradient flow may not exist even for short time
span.note: what this limits: the gradient-flow construction for general m: it MAY NOT EXIST EVEN FOR SHORT TIME
span.quote: may not exist even for short time

span.label: The surgery arguments, which the program needs, are deferred to another paper.
span.note: what this limits: the completeness of the programme as presented here: THE MORE TECHNICALLY COMPLICATED ARGUMENTS, RELATED TO THE SURGERY, WILL BE DISCUSSED ELSEWHERE
span.quote: The more technically complicated arguments, related to the surgery, will be discussed elsewhere.

span.label: The author could not establish Hamilton's expected boundedness of normalized curvature for eternal solutions.
span.note: what this limits: the eternal-solutions claim: WE HAVE NOT BEEN ABLE TO CONFIRM HAMILTON'S HOPE THAT THE SOLUTION THAT EXISTS FOR ALL TIME NECESSARILY HAS BOUNDED NORMALIZED CURVATURE
span.quote: We have not been able to confirm Hamilton’s hope that the solution that exists for all time t necessarily has bounded normalized curvature; still we are able to show that the region where this does not hold is locally collapsed with curvature bounded below; by our earlier (partly unpublished) work this is enough for topological conclusions.

span.label: No proof is given that the limiting construction yields a canonically defined Ricci flow through singularities.
span.note: what this limits: the canonical-flow-through-singularities claim: IT IS LIKELY THAT ... ONE WOULD GET A CANONICALLY DEFINED RICCI FLOW THROUGH SINGULARITIES, BUT AT THE MOMENT I DON'T HAVE A PROOF OF THAT
span.quote: It is likely that by passing to the limit in this construction one would get a canonically defined Ricci flow through singularities, but at the moment I don’t have a proof of that.

span.label: Details of the rigorous version of the shrinking-case argument are not supplied.
span.note: what this limits: the rigour of the shrinking-case argument as given: THIS ARGUMENT IS NOT HARD TO MAKE RIGOROUS; THE DETAILS ARE LEFT TO THE READER - the support is not in the paper
span.quote: This argument is not hard to make rigorous; the details are left to the reader.

span.label: The author states his own understanding is insufficient for the physics analogy invoked (Black Hole Thermodynamics).
span.note: what this limits: the physical analogy only: UNFORTUNATELY, THIS SUBJECT IS BEYOND MY UNDERSTANDING AT THE MOMENT - the Black Hole Thermodynamics parallel is offered without being vouched for
span.quote: Unfortunately, this subject is beyond my understanding at the moment.

span.label: The result the paper is famous for is presented as a brief sketch.
span.note: what this limits: the geometrization result attributed to this paper: what it contains at that point is described by the author as a brief sketch of the proof
span.quote: we give a brief sketch of the proof

span.label: The curvature fact the blow-up analysis rests on is imported from earlier work and holds in dimension three.
span.note: what this limits: the nonnegative-curvature property of blow-up limits used here: it rests on results of Ivey and Hamilton proved in dimension three, where large scalar curvature makes the negative part of the curvature tensor comparatively small
span.quote: However, Ivey [I] and Hamilton [H 4] proved that in dimension three, at the points where scalar curvature is large, the negative part of the curvature tensor is small compared to the scalar curvature, and therefore the blow-up limits have necessarily nonnegative sectional curvature

span.label: A formula of the paper's resembles a known one and moves in the opposite direction.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison of this reduced-volume formula with Huisken's monotonicity formula for mean curvature flow: the author states the two resemble each other but that here the monotonicity runs in the opposite direction
span.quote: Our formula for the reduced volume resembles the expression in Huisken monotonicity formula for the mean curvature flow [Hu]; however, in our case the monotonicity is in the opposite direction

span.label: importing entropy and monotonicity ideas from statistical physics to build monotonic functionals for the Ricci flow, used to resolve geometric and topological questions
span.quote: The interplay of statistical physics and (pseudo)-riemannian geometry occurs in the subject of Black Hole Thermodynamics

span.label: Ricci flow
span.quote: when it exists, it is just the Ricci flow, modified by a diffeomorphism

span.label: geometrization conjecture
span.quote: Thus, the implementation of Hamilton program would imply the geometrization conjecture for closed three-manifolds

span.label: Hamilton program
span.quote: Thus, the implementation of Hamilton program would imply the geometrization conjecture for closed three-manifolds.

span.label: reduced volume
span.quote: Our formula for the reduced volume resembles the expression in Huisken monotonicity formula for the mean curvature flow [Hu]; however, in our case the monotonicity is in the opposite direction

span.label: monotonicity formula
span.quote: resembles the expression in Huisken monotonicity formula for the mean curvature flow

span.label: the conjecture this paper is known for - NEVER NAMED IN IT: 'Poincare' occurs nowhere; what the paper addresses is the geometrization conjecture, from which the more famous result follows, so the absence is not a later coinage but a stronger claim standing in for a weaker one
span.quote: Thus, the implementation of Hamilton program would imply the geometrization conjecture for closed three-manifolds

span.label: monotonicity - RESEMBLING A KNOWN FORMULA AND RUNNING THE OTHER WAY: the reduced-volume expression looks like Huisken's for mean curvature flow, and the author states the direction of monotonicity is opposite, so matching the two on their form would join quantities that disagree in sign
span.quote: Our formula for the reduced volume resembles the expression in Huisken monotonicity formula for the mean curvature flow [Hu]; however, in our case the monotonicity is in the opposite direction

span.label: entropy - BY STATISTICAL ANALOGY, AND HEURISTIC: the monotonicity formula is interpreted in terms of the entropy of a canonical ensemble, and the author calls the connection to renormalization group flow heuristic rather than derived
span.quote: Heuristically, this statistical analogy is related to the description of the renormalization group flow, mentioned in the introduction: in the latter one obtains various quantities by averaging over higher energy states, whereas in the former those states are suppressed by the exponential factor

span.label: builds-on → Hamilton Ricci flow
span.quote: The Ricci flow equation, introduced by Richard Hamilton

span.label: builds-on → statistical physics / thermodynamics (entropy concepts)
span.quote: interplay of statistical physics and (pseudo)-riemannian geometry

span.label: builds-on → Hamilton's program for the Ricci flow and geometrization
span.quote: In this paper we carry out some details of Hamilton program.

span.label: builds-on → Hamilton's program (implication for the geometrization conjecture)
span.quote: Thus, the implementation of Hamilton program would imply the geometrization conjecture for closed three-manifolds.

span.label: extends → Ivey [I], no breathers theorem in dimension three
span.quote: 3.3* The no breathers theorem in dimension three was proved by Ivey [I]; in fact, he also ruled out nontrivial Ricci solitons; his proof uses the almost nonnegative curvature estimate, mentioned in the introduction.

span.label: builds-on → renormalization group flow picture from quantum field theory
span.quote: Anyway, this connection between the Ricci flow and the RG flow suggests that Ricci flow must be gradient-like; the present work confirms this expectation.

span.label: Hamilton program —causes→ geometrization conjecture
span.quote: Thus, the implementation of Hamilton program would imply the geometrization conjecture for closed three-manifolds

span.label: reduced volume —contrasted-with→ monotonicity formula
span.quote: Our formula for the reduced volume resembles the expression in Huisken monotonicity formula for the mean curvature flow [Hu]; however, in our case the monotonicity is in the opposite direction

span.label: Where singularities (necks) form, one performs SURGERY — cutting the neck and gluing caps — then continues the Ricci flow.
span.quote: it is natural to make a surgery by cutting open the neck and gluing small caps to each of the boundaries, and then to continue running the Ricci flow

span.label: Ricci soliton
span.note: about this quote: QUOTE REPAIRED (Q-697): the extractor split a hyphen-space and the quote was recorded faithfully with the damage in it, which made it unanchorable. The repaired string is an EXACT SUBSTRING of the staged text - that is why it was accepted, not because a rule produced it. The text as originally recorded is kept in `evidence_as_extracted`.
span.quote: are called Ricci solitons. (Thus, if one considers Ricci flow as a dynamical system on the space of riemannian metrics modulo diffeomorphism

span.label: surgery (on the flow)
span.quote: make a surgery by cutting open the neck and gluing small caps to each of the boundaries, and then to continue running the Ricci flow
